title: Everyday Grammar: A Demo Course
subtitle: Four short units of English grammar
about: This short course shows how English Drill Book works. Each unit has a page that explains one point of grammar and a page of exercises. The answers are at the back of the book.

Read the explanation first, then do the exercises. Write your answers in the app or in a notebook, and check them with the key. The companion book, Everyday Grammar: Demo Drills, has more practice on the same four topics.

explanation.text: We use the verb be to say who people are, where they are and what they are like. Be has three forms in the present: am, is and are.
To make a negative, put not after am, is or are. In speech we usually use the short forms isn't and aren't. There is no short form of am not: say I'm not.

lines: I'm not late, the bus is early.
The shop isn't open on Mondays.
Our cats aren't in the house.

explanation.text: In a question the verb comes before the person or thing. A question word, such as where or how, comes first of all.

explanation.title: Short answers
explanation.text: Answer a yes or no question with the person and the verb: Yes, I am. No, she isn't. In a positive short answer, do not use the short form: Yes, we are, not Yes, we're.

exercises.task: Complete the sentences with am, is or are.

items.prompt: I ___ from a small town by the sea.
Omar and Priya ___ in the garden.
I ___ hungry. Is there any bread?
My phone is in my bag.
accept: My phone is not in my bag
Kofi and Nell are not friends

units.title: Present simple: I work, she works

explanation.text: We use the present simple for things that are true in general and for things we do again and again: habits, routines and timetables.
After he, she and it, add -s to the verb. Verbs that end in -ch, -sh, -s, -x or -o add -es: watch, watches; go, goes. A consonant and y becomes -ies: study, studies. Have becomes has.
Negatives and questions use do or does and the plain verb, with no -s.

lines: I don't eat meat. Bruno doesn't drive.
Do you like tea? Does she live here?

explanation.title: Careful
explanation.text: Does already shows that the person is he, she or it, so the verb after it stays plain: Does he work? not Does he works?

exercises.task: Write the verb in brackets in the present simple.

items.prompt: My aunt ___ in a small town. (live)
The baby ___ a lot at night. (cry)
Dasha ___ two cats and a parrot. (have)
___ the train stop at this station?

exercises.task: Read about Omar. Write the text again with the verbs in the present simple.
exercises.prompt: Omar (live) in a flat near the river. He (get) up at seven and (have) a quick breakfast. Then he (walk) to the library, where he (look) after old maps. In the evening he (cook) dinner and (call) his sister.
exercises.model: Omar lives in a flat near the river. He gets up at seven and has a quick breakfast. Then he walks to the library, where he looks after old maps. In the evening he cooks dinner and calls his sister.

explanation.text: Use a or an before a singular noun when you talk about one thing, or when you say what something or somebody is.

explanation.title: Which one?
rows: a cup, a lemon, a house
an egg, an onion, an idea

explanation.text: The sound decides, not the letter. Hour starts with a vowel sound, because the h is silent, so we say an hour. Uniform and university start with a y sound, so we say a uniform.
Use a or an when you say what job somebody does.

explanation.title: Careful
explanation.text: Do not use a or an with a plural noun: apples, not an apples. And do not leave it out before a job: I am a nurse, not I am nurse.

items.prompt: Can I have ___ glass of water?

exercises.task: Write a or an before each word.
What do these people do? Write a sentence about each person with a or an.

items.prompt: Priya / doctor. She works at the hospital in the centre of town.
Sven / actor. He is in a play at the theatre this month.
my uncle / farmer. He has sheep, hens and a very old tractor.
Nell / architect. She draws plans for new schools and libraries.
Bruno / taxi driver. He knows every street in the city.
my cousin / artist. She paints large pictures of the sea.
Kofi / engineer. He builds bridges over rivers and roads.
Dasha / police officer. She works at night in the old part of town.
Ivo / waiter. He brings coffee and cake to the people at the tables.
my neighbour / English teacher. Her students are adults.
accept: My neighbour is an English teacher

explanation.text: Use there is and there are to say that something exists, or to say where it is. The noun after them decides which one you use.

explanation.title: Positive
rows: There is a bank in our street.
There are two parks near the school.

explanation.text: The short form of there is is there's. For negatives use isn't and aren't. In questions, is or are comes first.

lines: There isn't a lift in this building.
Are there any eggs in the fridge?
Yes, there are. No, there aren't.

explanation.title: Some and any
explanation.text: With a plural noun, use some in positive sentences and any in negatives and questions: There are some cups. There aren't any spoons. Are there any forks?

exercises.task: Complete the sentences with there is or there are.

items.prompt: ___ a big tree in our garden.
___ lots of people at the station.

exercises.task: Write four sentences about your room. Use there is and there are.
exercises.prompt: Ideas: a bed, a window, a desk, some books, a lamp, some pictures, a plant.
exercises.sample: There is a bed next to the window. There are some books on the desk. There isn't a television. There are two pictures on the wall.
